extracted.intended_audience: grade-5 teachers, site coordinators, test administrators, and essay scoring teams
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures and scoring criteria for a grade-5 multi-day student writing assessment, including test administration rules, permitted resources, collection/roster procedures, a holistic 6-point rubric, and a six-trait analytic (six-point) scoring guide. Also includes teacher-survey scales about writing instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Holistic rubric (6-point)
rubrics_metrics.description: A single overall score from 6 (highest) to 1 (lowest) describing overall mastery of writing on the task.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Score of 6: demonstrates clear and consistent mastery (may have a few minor errors). Typically: effectively and insightfully addresses topic/task; outstanding development of a theme with appropriate supporting elements; well organized and clearly focused with coherence and smooth progression; skillful use of language with varied, accurate, apt vocabulary; meaningful variety in sentence structure; free of most errors in grammar, usage, mechanics.

Score of 5: reasonably consistent mastery with occasional errors. Typically: effectively addresses topic/task; strong development of a theme with appropriate support; well organized and focused; facility in language use with appropriate vocabulary; variety in sentence structure; generally free of most errors.

Score of 4: adequate mastery with lapses in quality. Typically: addresses topic/task and competent development using adequate support; generally organized and focused with some coherence; adequate but inconsistent facility in language and vocabulary; some variety in sentence structure; some errors in grammar/usage/mechanics.

Score of 3: developing mastery; marked by one or more weaknesses (inconsistent development/support, limited organization/focus, weak vocabulary/word choice, lack of sentence variety, accumulation of errors).

Score of 2: little mastery; flawed by one or more severe weaknesses (vague/limited addressing of topic, poor organization/coherence, very limited vocabulary or incorrect word choice, frequent sentence-structure problems, errors that obscure meaning).

Score of 1: very little or no mastery (barely addresses topic, little or no development, disorganized/unfocused, fundamental vocabulary errors, severe sentence-structure flaws, pervasive errors that interfere with meaning).

Scoring rule: Essays not written on the essay assignment will receive a score of zero.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytic rubrics (six-trait/six-point) — general
rubrics_metrics.description: The study uses six separate analytic trait rubrics, each scored 6 (highest) to 1 (lowest). Traits comprise Ideas/Content (development), Organization, Voice, Word Choice, Sentence Fluency, and Conventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each analytic trait is scored independently on a six-point scale. Detailed descriptors are provided trait by trait (see individual trait entries). The analytic rubrics are used by scoring teams to evaluate specific dimensions of writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ideas/Content (development) — analytic trait
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluates clarity/focus of topic and depth/quality of development and support for the central theme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Score 6: extremely clear/focused; relevant anecdotes/details enrich central theme. (A) Topic narrow/manageable. (B) Relevant, telling details go beyond obvious. (C) Accurate, precise details support main ideas; appropriate resources provide credible support. (D) Writing shows experience/fresh/original ideas. (E) Reader’s questions anticipated and answered. (F) Writing makes connections/insights about significance.

Score 5: ideas/content well marked by detail and information; topic focused though could narrow; more than half the time details/support are clear and relevant; credible details present; some new ways of thinking presented; reader mostly satisfied.

Score 4: development basic or general; topic defined though broad; support attempted but insufficiently fleshed out; ideas reasonably clear but may lack personalization/expansion; some showing but reliance on general examples.

Score 3: reader can understand main ideas though broad/simplistic; support incidental/confusing; details limited; reliance on telling rather than showing; reader may have many questions.

Score 2: no one main idea stands out; support sporadic; general sense of idea present but without significant detail.

Score 1: no clear sense of purpose; topic not settled; information limited/unclear; text repetitious or disconnected.  (Guidance includes subpoints A–F across score levels describing typical problems or strengths.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Organization — analytic trait
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluates how effectively the order, structure, and presentation of information enhance and move the reader through the text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Score 6: organization enhances and showcases central idea or theme; compelling order/structure; inviting introduction and satisfying conclusion; thoughtful transitions; logical/effective sequencing; well-controlled pacing; title (if required) captures central theme.

Score 5: organization smooth with only a few small bumps; goes beyond obvious beginning/conclusion; transitions logical though may lack originality; sequencing sensible; pacing under control.

Score 4: organizational structure strong enough to move the reader without too much confusion; recognizable introduction and conclusion though may not create strong anticipation; transitions often work but sometimes fuzzy; sequencing makes sense but not fully under control; pacing fairly controlled.

Score 3: organization somewhat problematic and slows reader’s engagement; introductions/conclusions may be cliché; transitions repetitive/misleading; structure may dominate ideas; pacing issues.

Score 2: piece needs a great deal of work to be effective; few moments give coherence.

Score 1: lacks clear direction; ideas disjointed; sequencing/pacing severely flawed.  (Descriptors include subpoints A–F for specific features at high/low levels.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Voice — analytic trait (listed)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the six analytic traits in the scoring guide; evaluates the writer’s individuality, tone, and authorial presence appropriate to purpose/audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trait is part of the six-trait, six-point analytic scoring guide. Detailed level descriptors for Voice appear in the full analytic rubric (not included in this appendix chunk). Scorers evaluate authenticity, engagement, appropriateness of tone, and the writer’s ability to connect with the reader.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word Choice — analytic trait (listed)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the six analytic traits focusing on vocabulary, precision, and appropriateness of words chosen to express ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the six-trait analytic rubric. Scoring considers aptness, variety, accuracy, and richness of vocabulary; details and examples in the complete rubric (not fully reproduced in this chunk).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentence Fluency — analytic trait (listed)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the six analytic traits assessing sentence structure, rhythm, and flow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the six-trait analytic rubric. Scorers consider variety and control of sentence structures, sentence rhythm, and readability; detailed descriptors are in the full rubric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conventions — analytic trait (listed)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the six analytic traits assessing grammar, usage, punctuation, and mechanics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the six-trait analytic rubric. Scoring considers frequency and severity of errors and whether errors interfere with meaning; full-level descriptors appear in the complete rubric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring rule: off-topic essays receive zero
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy for essays that are not written on the assigned prompt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any essay not written on the essay assignment will receive a score of zero (distinct from 1–6 holistic scores).

rubrics_metrics.name: Test administration — general guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: High-level rules for administering the writing assessments to students over three consecutive days and maintaining testing integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessments are completed over three consecutive days during 45–50 minute uninterrupted periods; notify study center if schedule problems occur. Teachers give brief instructions but students write on their own without teacher or peer assistance in planning, drafting, revising, or editing. Teachers may reread prompts to individual students but must not suggest content or proofread. Students proceed at their own pace; early finishers should have quiet reading materials or other planned activities. All study-group students complete the assessment in English. Students may use a dictionary and thesaurus of the type normally available in the school; they may not use handouts or locally developed materials beyond word-definition/spelling guides, nor reference sources (textbooks, encyclopedias) or peer editing. Students should use accommodations/modifications only if specified in their IEP or 504 Plan. Students may not use a computer/word processor unless specified in IEP/504.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administering the student writing assessment — step-by-step procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific procedural steps for Day 1 and follow-up days for distributing, conducting, collecting, and reporting the writing assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Before class: confirm each study-group student has a Writing Booklet with name on cover; if missing, write student name on Classroom Roster and on a booklet with the same code number. Review General Writing Assessment Guidelines and instructions. Day 1: hand out booklets; ensure desks clear and pens/pencils available; read boxed directions verbatim to all students; follow STEP ONE (Planning — use planning page), STEP TWO (Write rough draft on designated draft pages), STEP THREE (Revise, edit, recopy final copy on Final Copy pages, write final in black ink, keep final neat). Do not allow taking booklets home. Collect booklets at end of assessment period and store securely.

Days 2–3: continue as Day 1; read verbatim box text reminding students to use planning/draft/final pages and allowed editing tools (no teacher/student help). Collect booklets at end of each day; Day 3: return booklets to Site Coordinator; check all booklets for completion and presence of drafts/final copies—if missing, add explanatory notes on final copy. On Classroom Roster, complete Status, Accommodations, and Modifications columns (use coded Status values; code “1–Assessment completed” for completed). Mark Y/N for accommodations/modifications used during pretest. Ensure roster entries for grade, sex, ethnicity. Place Classroom Roster and all Writing Booklets in Classroom Packet and return to Site Coordinator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student booklet instructions (in-booklet directions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructions given to students in the sample Student Writing Project booklet about the prompt, planning, drafting, revising, and final copy conventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompt example: 'Think of a skill you have learned that has made your life easier or more fun. Write a letter telling about your skill, explain how you learned it, and why you think it is important.' Students told to use PLANNING page, write draft on DRAFT pages, mark revisions/edits on draft pages, write final copy in BLACK INK on FINAL COPY pages, and not to write on specified non-writing pages. Planning page and draft/final pages are positioned to make copying final easier. Explicit reminders to keep final copy neat and to turn booklets in at the end of the period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowed and prohibited resources during assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarification of what students may and may not use during the writing assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed: dictionary and thesaurus of the type normally available in the school, rereading of prompt by teacher for individual students, classroom editing tools (but not teacher/student assistance). Prohibited: handouts or locally developed handouts beyond word-definition/spelling guides; textbooks, encyclopedias, almanacs, other reference sources; peer editing. Computers/word processors prohibited unless specified in IEP/504. Accommodations/modifications allowed only as part of a student’s official IEP or 504 Plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teacher survey purpose, confidentiality, and rating scale
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructions for teachers completing the Teacher Survey on Writing Instruction including confidentiality assurances and the response scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: to understand how teachers teach writing and what classroom activities students engage in; not for teacher evaluation. Confidentiality: responses used only for statistical purposes; reports will summarize findings across sample and will not associate responses with a specific district or individual, except as required by law. Response rating scale for items about emphasis: 0 Not emphasized at all; 1–4 increasing emphasis; 5 Emphasized often or strongly; 6 Emphasized very often and strongly. (The survey estimates ~30 minutes to complete and includes OMB control number.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructional strategy scale: Teaching the language of rubrics for writing assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: A named teacher-instruction scale measuring use of trait/rubric language in instruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Survey items included on this scale: items 6, 7, 19, 26, 29, 37, 45 (see Teacher Survey item text for full item wording). Used in creating scale scores in the Fidelity of Implementation section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructional strategy scale: Reading and scoring papers and justifying the scores
rubrics_metrics.description: Scale measuring teachers’ practices in reading/scoring student work and explaining scoring decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Survey items included on this scale: items 1, 10, 22, 30, 43.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructional strategy scale: Teaching focused revision strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Scale measuring instruction that emphasizes teaching specific revision strategies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Survey items included: items 8, 21, 25, 33, 38.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructional strategy scale: Modeling participation in the writing process
rubrics_metrics.description: Scale measuring teacher modeling of their own writing process for students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Survey items included: items 2, 11, 20, 34.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructional strategy scale: Having students read and analyze materials that demonstrate varying writing quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Scale measuring use of mentor texts and analytic reading to teach writing quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Survey items included: items 9, 18, 31.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructional strategy scale: Giving students writing assignments to respond to effective prompts
rubrics_metrics.description: Scale measuring use of prompts that clearly identify audience and purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Survey items included: items 17, 28, 35, 41.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructional strategy scale: Weaving writing lessons into other subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Scale measuring integration of writing instruction across subject areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Survey items included: items 5, 12, 13, 42.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructional strategy scale: Teaching students to set goals and monitor their progress
rubrics_metrics.description: Scale measuring instruction that fosters student self-monitoring and goal-setting for writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Survey items included: items 16, 36, 39, 40, 44.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructional strategy scale: Integrating learning goals for writing into curriculum planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Scale measuring alignment of writing learning goals with curriculum planning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Survey items included: items 3, 14, 23, 32.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructional strategy scale: Teaching ways to structure nonfiction writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Scale measuring instruction on organizing nonfiction structures (sequential, cause/effect, problem/solution, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Survey items included: items 4, 15, 24, 27.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teacher grading methods for student writing (survey response options)
rubrics_metrics.description: Options teachers selected to describe how they grade students’ writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Survey question lists four grading approaches: (1) Single grade for whole assignment; (2) Single grade for whole assignment with feedback comments; (3) Separate grades for different writing skills; (4) Separate grades for different writing skills with feedback comments. Teachers were asked to circle the number before the one answer that best describes their practice.
